approved: Administrative and Judicial Review Legislation Amendment Bill 2026

Moved the second reading of a bill to improve the efficiency of the Administrative Review Tribunal and the Federal Circuit and Family Court in managing migration and other caseloads. Proposed oral reasons in some matters, identity verification for prescribed migration reviews, and safeguards for social security, veterans, disability and aged-care cases.

Declared that, unless otherwise ordered, the Social Security and Other Legislation Amendment (Technical Changes No. 2) Bill 2026 and Administrative and Judicial Review Legislation Amendment Bill 2026 be referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration after debate on each bill's second-reading motion is adjourned.

Argued that the Administrative and Judicial Review Legislation Amendment Bill 2026 was needed to improve an underperforming Administrative Review Tribunal and address its backlog. Supported expanded registrar powers, streamlined migration review procedures, identity verification requirements, oral decisions in some migration matters, and stronger reporting, while saying the Coalition would support the bill.

Supported the Administrative and Judicial Review Legislation Amendment Bill 2026, arguing it would improve administrative review by reducing unnecessary written reasons, standardising migration applications, expanding registrar powers with safeguards, correcting obvious errors, and introducing identity verification for prescribed migration and protection matters while retaining flexibility for genuine applicants.

Supported the Administrative and Judicial Review Legislation Amendment Bill 2026, describing amendments to give the Administrative Review Tribunal greater flexibility such as delivering reasons for decisions orally, streamlining migration review processes and adding identity-check requirements, and cited a Melbourne constituent whose immigration case took from 2020 to 2025 to resolve; the government opposed the member for Kooyong's second-reading amendment and the bill passed its second reading.
